digest.component_or_area: CI test suite performance and optimization
propositions: The newest three qualifying successful full-route Gerrit Verify runs averaged 24m58s (range 22m47s–26m14s), within the 20–30 minute objective, with no individual test phase exceeding 30s on macOS or in the CI sample.

Gerrit 1817 merged the removal of 19 proven OS/Python-invariant repository-policy nodes from macOS and Ubuntu 3.11/3.12, retaining them only in Ubuntu 3.13, projected to save ~8s macOS critical-path and 24.84 aggregate runner-seconds without adding new jobs or setup overhead.

The normalized >=1.0s inventory union contains 501 unique test phases (403 from exhaustive local macOS default, 73 from exhaustive local integration, plus CI top-25 observations), categorized by family (Git concurrency, import/packaging, analyzers, gates, deployment, etc.) with each phase assigned a keep/refactor/equivalence-research disposition and coverage rationale.

No CI setup/call/teardown phase was observed above 30s in either the three-run sample (max 22.63s) or the exhaustive current-main local census (max 15.62s default, 21.96s integration), indicating no single slow test is the measured completion long pole.

Research opportunities exist for external analyzers (lead-unpleasing-kitten), partial-clone fixture scaling (reasonable-kingsize-polliwog), and show-under-write-burst consolidation (rival-ammoniacal-crustacean), conditional on fault-seeded equivalence proof and rejection search; real Git/concurrency/process/platform behavior must remain on macOS.
